criteria.extend_compiler_head: Touch the other lane's runtime/platform/html.ts so compiler-owned head rendering appends the paired script, threading the pairing into createHTML and the generated state initializer. Script tags stay inside head-owned bytes, but the change spans a lane boundary and alters a factory contract.
criteria.inject_document: When the active build is paired, the HTTP layer splices a single `<script type="module" src="<report-selected digest URL>">` directly ahead of `</body>` in text/html document payloads. Payloads without a body marker, non-HTML answers, HEAD traffic, and all unpaired builds keep their exact bytes.
criteria.serve_bytes_only: Ship the checked JS/map/table bytes and note the chosen URL in the report, yet bind no page in UP18; page binding moves to follow-up work. Minimal footprint, but the explicit page-binding acceptance clause remains unsatisfied.

page_binding.instructions: By which route should served pages arrive at the report-selected paired script URL, when Can authors cannot mint script elements and html.ts is owned elsewhere?

criteria.carry_forward: Duplicate every superseded digest byte into each fresh server generation and stamp its replacement moment in the emitted table. Generations remain self-describing, yet embedded wall-clock values destroy byte-identical rebuilds, while stamping the earlier publication moment shortens the guaranteed window.
criteria.durable_ledger: Persist superseded bytes in a dist-level content-addressed directory (dist/assets/<digest><ext>) and track each route's replacement moment in an atomically replaced ledger (dist/assets.json). Requests succeed while now minus replacedAt does not exceed seven days; each build reaps expired rows under the project lock, leaving generations free of timestamps.
criteria.pin_generations: Retain outdated server generations and answer old routes out of them, with pruning gated on age. This avoids a fresh store at the price of serve-time discovery across generations and the hazard of exposing staged sets that never became current.

retention.instructions: Which retention shape keeps superseded digest URLs alive for at least seven days across restart, cleanup, and parallel builds without disturbing byte-identical rebuilds?

criteria.full_reaudit: Re-derive browserBuildId from the manifest's files array, re-hash every file from newly read generation bytes, confirm the generation manifest.json linkage, execute the complete post-bundle AuditBundle again (references, map pairing, table structure, canaries, banned operations), match lock and lockedInstances against the server graph, and re-read the browser inputs right before atomic selection.
criteria.hashes_and_lock_only: Re-derive browserBuildId, re-hash every file, and match lock plus lockedInstances, while accepting the browser build's earlier audit for references, maps, table structure, and canaries rather than repeating it during the server build.

verify_scope.instructions: How deep should server-build verification of the given browser manifest run before the paired set is published?

state.browser_output: A checked browser generation emits browser/browser.js (entry point with the canonical `//# sourceMappingURL=browser.js.map` tail), browser/browser.js.map, diagnostics/table.json, and browser/manifest.json. That manifest (schemaVersion 1, kind can.browser-manifest) records browserBuildId (SHA-256 across the can-browser-bundle-v1 domain and the files array), entry, table, per-file path plus sha256 plus route triples, toolchain, inputs, lock, and lockedInstances. Public routes follow /__can/assets/<sha256>.js with .js.map and .json counterparts. Generation content is content-addressed and frozen, while dist/builds/<id>/manifest.json pins all file digests.
state.mandate: Can serves no external users, so backwards compatibility carries no weight. UP18 joins a checked browser bundle to a Bun server build via `canlc build --target bun --browser-manifest <file> <server-project>`. The server build confirms the browser build ID, the common locked snapshot, the asset graph, and all hashes, writes the precise browser build ID plus digests into its verified report, and flips the full matched asset set into place atomically; unsuccessful rebuilds retain the earlier set. Your role is mechanism advice grounded solely in this evidence. Source inspection and code execution are unavailable to you.
state.ownership: This worker controls compiler/main.go, driver build/report/output inputs, runtime/platform/assets.ts, runtime/platform/server.ts, and tight asset/entry adjustments within compiler/internal/emit (declared at handoff). compiler/internal/check stays effectively sealed, runtime/platform/html.ts answers to a different lane, and runtime/catalogue.ts answers to the coordinator. Designs demanding another Can operation, catalogue row, checker revision, or html.ts revision step over an ownership line.
state.page_constraint: Two independent gates block authored scripts: project Snapshot refuses .js/.map manifest assets, and the HTML author tag vocabulary contains no script tag (src belongs to img alone). Can-authored pages close with </body></html>, whereas action fragments omit any body marker. The active CSP already enforces script-src 'self' without inline script or unsafe-eval, admitting a same-origin src-only module tag as-is.
state.race_duty: Checks must bind precisely the bytes that ship: browser files may shift between checking and publishing, and parallel builds contend for the dist. Flipping the report together with the whole asset table is indivisible, and every check failure keeps the previous verified set live. Each build already holds a single exclusive project lock and publishes through atomic renames.
state.retention_duty: Every superseded digest URL keeps returning its exact bytes for a minimum of seven days past replacement, surviving server restart, prune-style cleanup, and parallel builds. Same inputs must regenerate identical bytes since build identity derives from content. Wall-clock values frozen into a generation fracture that identity; mutable dist metadata such as current.json lives beyond the content hash.
state.server_output: A server generation freezes the $canAssetTable JSON ({htmx, project[]}) inside program/state.ts and stores asset bytes at assets/<digest>/<name>. dist/current.json crowns the production generation indivisibly. The asset layer serves exact table routes alone, re-checks each content digest per request, and stamps every answer with the shared content-security-policy.
